title: Every shell-command denial names both shells, and a check refuses a settings file where one has no twin

looked_in: every committed .claude/settings.json at HEAD, outside the imported autofocus tree and the rejected fixtures: deny and ask lists, counted by tool
contracts/validate.py for any check that reads PowerShell entries: none
the root CLAUDE.md's paragraph on which denials are inert

changes.change: A check over every committed .claude/settings.json: each Bash(<pattern>) in deny or ask has a PowerShell(<pattern>) beside it in the same list, and the reverse. A missing twin is a FAIL naming the file and the line. It checks that both shells are named, not that the two patterns stop the same commands. The commands differ between shells, so whether a twin is sufficient stays the owner's judgement, and the check's message says so.
One rejected group: a settings file with a Bash command denial and no PowerShell twin. Watched being accepted before the check exists.
Twin Bash(python3*hardware*) with PowerShell, and name python as well as python3, since python3 is not Python on the Windows computers.
Already in that seat's working copy when this was drafted: 13 PowerShell twins. Its landing is a member of this proposal's proof.
One sentence where tool denials are called not inert: a command denial names one shell tool, and on Windows the PowerShell tool needs its own line.

fixtures.path: console-office-20261017-1's two-command probe, before and after 950bff0c
fixtures.watched_failing_before: Bash `echo guard-probe mm-real` denied; PowerShell `Write-Output "guard-probe mm-real"` ran (reported)
fixtures.watched_passing_after: after 950bff0c, in the same running session: Bash denied, PowerShell denied (reported). So PowerShell(...) command denials are honoured. Not yet seen from a restarted session.

already_running: every session rooted at a folder whose settings change: settings are read at session start, so a running session keeps the old denials until it restarts
reach.how_they_learn: The owner of each settings file tells the sessions rooted there to restart. The check refuses the next commit that adds a one-shell denial anywhere, which is where a new one would be written.
reach.use_site: the commit gate, for new denials; a restart, for running sessions

notes: Measured narrower than first reported: two files hold command denials, not all of them. The check is still worth having, because the next file to add one is where the gap would reopen. Settings denials are a second layer: the safety rules are enforced by deterministic code in the operator, which this does not touch. Nothing here is in 8.3 rule 2's core. A settings fix reaches only sessions started after it, which the root CLAUDE.md names as a class of its own. So the reach above asks each owner to say who must restart. Progress: the console's twins landed at 950bff0c (manager-console-office-20261017-1), and the CLAUDE.md sentence at 36416ebb (architecture-20261007-1). The check, its fixture and the bridge twin are still open.
